READING PASSAGE 2

You should spend about 20 minutes on Questions 14–26, which are based on Reading Passage 2 below.

Australia's Camouflaged Creatures

Many species of animal in Australia protect themselves by using camouflage — a way of ‘hiding’ by blending into the surroundings.

A Most species use camouflage to some extent. If they are convincing, they survive to pass their genes on to future generations. After generations of natural selection, animals can develop astonishingly complex camouflage techniques, manipulating shape, colour and movement. ‘The principle of camouflage is to make it economically unviable for a predator to pursue a particular species of prey,’ explains Professor Mark Elgar of the University of Melbourne. ‘Camouflage increases the search time and, as a consequence, the predator will simply target another species, either because it doesn’t see the camouflaged individual or it just finds something more obvious to do.’

B The easiest way for an animal to disguise itself is to be invisible in its surroundings. To that end, stick and leaf insects have evolved complex camouflage to hide themselves from predators. Many have the texture of sticks or dry leaves, while others imitate living foliage, even the veins in a leaf. Some insects develop blemishes to match the spots caused by disease. A convincing appearance only works if its owner also acts the part, so during the day the creature using this type of camouflage keeps motionless, or sways like a dead leaf in the breeze. If disturbed, it falls to the ground and stays still. Entomologist Paul Zborowski, who has spent decades photographing inconspicuous creatures, rates the desert insects of Central Australia as the most convincingly disguised creatures he’s seen. ‘It’s an incredibly old habitat, so the creatures have had a long time to adapt,’ Zborowski explains. Most of them behave like stones and don’t move all day, feeding only at night.

C A tawny frogmouth sitting motionless on a stump also illustrates the importance of pairing a persuasive costume with behaviour. Professor Gisela Kaplan of the University of New England in Australia says the frogmouth’s skill at camouflaging is learned behaviour. While adopting a pose may be a reflex of the bird, and can be observed in a hatchling’s first week, the ability to choose a backdrop which matches its colouration does not develop for 4–6 months. When the chicks land, they are usually highly conspicuous, and their parents try to signal to them to move to a safe location.

D Fixed camouflage is only good against a relatively unchanging environment, so some animals, such as the cuttlefish, have evolved an adaptable disguise. The cuttlefish can almost instantly change its colour, pattern and texture to match its surroundings, using specialised cells and muscles. On Queensland’s reefs, scientists have been studying another ocean dweller that uses colour change, although not to blend into the surroundings. Dr Karen Cheney, from the University of Queensland, says the bluestriped fangblenny alters its colouration to mimic other species of fish, allowing it to travel with them and benefit from safety in numbers. Its most impressive impersonation is of the black-with-neon-blue-striped cleaner wrasse, which eats the parasites on larger fish. Not only does the fangblenny benefit from the reduced predation that comes with the wrasse’s beneficial relationships with other fish, but the disguise also lets it get closer to prey. It darts out from the safety of the wrasse’s cleaning station to nip at unsuspecting fish passing by, but it doesn’t attack those coming to be cleaned.

E The most famous form of mimicry, however, is for defence, not attack. Batesian mimicry refers to animals that gain protection from predators by imitating a dangerous organism, often using conspicuous colours. The nineteenth-century naturalist Henry Bates first suggested this camouflage technique after noticing that several Amazonian butterfly species looked the same. The technique was later called after him. In Australian waters, the harmless harlequin snake eel sports the same black and white bandings as the highly toxic yellow-lipped sea krait, ensuring no predator will attack. However, the success of Batesian mimicry depends on the ratio of mimics to originals. If a predator encounters too many that are edible, it will just assume none of the animals with those markings are dangerous, explains Martyn Robinson, an educational naturalist with the Australian Museum.

F An imitation of a more dangerous creature needn’t be exact, just enough to make potential predators hesitate. The hawk moth caterpillar has markings resembling a snake’s eyes on its abdomen. When confronted, the caterpillar pulls its head in and the ‘eyes’ flash open. Whether the potential predator thinks it has seen a snake, or is simply startled, is unclear, but the outcome is that the caterpillar lives to see another day.

G In Queensland’s tablelands, the chameleon gecko has another way of making predators hesitate. Its body is brown, but its tail is banded in black and white. Robinson explains that if attacked, the chameleon gecko will drop off its tail, which will wriggle around on the ground. Many lizards do this, but in the case of the chameleon gecko the tail bones actually rub against one another, so it squeaks. ‘The predator is, of course, thoroughly absorbed by this black-and-white-striped, wriggling, squeaking thing on the ground, and the gecko can sneak away,’ Robinson says. It’s a one-time-only trick: the regrown tail is brown, the same as the gecko’s body. Such precise disguise and elaborate trickery illustrate the limitless possibilities of nature. But, as Robinson points out, only the most successful illusionists are here to tell the tale.

Questions 14–18

Reading Passage 2 has seven sections, A–G.

Which section contains the following information?

Write the correct letter, A–G, in boxes 14–18 on your answer sheet.

ABCDEFG
14 a species that indicates to its young to move to a place where they are less visible
15 an instance where sound is used to help an animal escape
16 a creature that can use camouflage to match a range of different backgrounds
17 a claim that the majority of animals disguise themselves in some way
18 examples of animals that use camouflage to look like plants

Questions 19–23

Look at the following statements (Questions 19–23) and the list of people below.

Match each statement with the correct person, A–F.

Write the correct letter, A–F, in boxes 19–23 on your answer sheet.

19 one species has a camouflage tactic that is not present from birth.

20 species that live in an ancient environment have become very effective at camouflaging themselves.

21 part of an animal is left behind to distract predators.

22 if it takes too long to find one kind of prey, animals will look for an alternative source of food.

23 camouflage can involve copying a threatening type of animal.

List of people
A Professor Mark Elgar
B Paul Zborowski
C Professor Gisela Kaplan
D Dr Karen Cheney
E Henry Bates
F Martyn Robinson

Questions 24–26

Complete the summary below.

Choose ONE WORD ONLY from the passage for each answer.

The bluestriped fangblenny

Dr Karen Cheney studies the bluestriped fangblenny on 24 off Queensland's coast. She found that the fangblenny was able to make itself resemble other fish by adjusting its colouration. The fangblenny impersonates the striped cleaner wrasse, a fish that is welcomed by other species as it gets rid of their 25 . The fangblenny can approach its 26 without drawing the attention of predators or disturbing the work of the striped cleaner wrasse.

passageNotes.label: Paragraph A
passageNotes.text: 大多数物种在某种程度上都会使用伪装。如果伪装令人信服，它们就能生存并将基因传递给后代。经过数代自然选择，动物可以发展出令人惊叹的复杂伪装技术，操控形状、颜色和动作。墨尔本大学的Mark Elgar教授解释道：“伪装的原理是让捕食者追逐某一特定猎物在经济上变得不划算。伪装增加了搜索时间，因此捕食者会转而攻击其他物种，要么是因为它看不到伪装的个体，要么是因为它只是发现了更容易捕捉的猎物。”

passageNotes.label: Paragraph B
passageNotes.text: 动物伪装自己的最简单方式是在周围环境中隐形。为此，竹节虫和叶蝉进化出了复杂的伪装来躲避捕食者。许多竹节虫具有树枝或干树叶的质地，另一些则模仿活的树叶，甚至模仿叶脉。有些昆虫会长出斑点以匹配疾病造成的斑痕。令人信服的外表只有在它的拥有者也配合行动时才有效，因此在白天，使用这种伪装的动物保持静止不动，或者像枯叶一样在微风中摇摆。如果受到惊扰，它会掉到地上保持不动。几十年来一直在拍摄不起眼生物的昆虫学家Paul Zborowski，将澳大利亚中部的沙漠昆虫评为他见过的伪装最令人信服的生物。Zborowski解释说：“这是一个极其古老的栖息地，所以这些生物有很长时间来适应。”它们大多数像石头一样整天不动，只在夜间进食。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph C
passageNotes.text: 一只茶色蛙嘴夜鹰静止不动地蹲在树桩上，也说明了将有说服力的外表与行为相结合的重要性。澳大利亚新英格兰大学的Gisela Kaplan教授说，蛙嘴夜鹰的伪装技巧是后天习得的行为。虽然摆出某种姿势可能是鸟类的本能反射，在孵化第一周就能观察到，但选择与其体色相匹配的背景的能力需要4到6个月才能发展出来。当幼鸟落地时，它们通常非常显眼，它们的父母会试图示意它们移动到安全的位置。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph D
passageNotes.text: 固定的伪装只在相对不变的环境中有效，因此一些动物，如墨鱼，进化出了可适应的伪装。墨鱼可以利用专门的细胞和肌肉，几乎瞬间改变其颜色、图案和质地以匹配周围环境。在昆士兰的珊瑚礁上，科学家们一直在研究另一种使用颜色变化的海洋生物，尽管目的不是融入周围环境。昆士兰大学的Karen Cheney博士说，蓝纹尖牙鳚改变其体色以模仿其他鱼类物种，使它能够与它们同行，并从群体安全中获益。它最令人印象深刻的模仿对象是黑底霓虹蓝条纹的清洁濑鱼，这种鱼吃大鱼身上的寄生虫。尖牙鳚不仅从濑鱼与其他鱼类的互利关系所带来的减少捕食中获益，而且这种伪装还让它能够更接近猎物。它从濑鱼清洁站的安全位置冲出来，咬一口毫无防备地经过的鱼，但它不会攻击那些前来被清洁的鱼。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph E
passageNotes.text: 然而，最著名的拟态形式是用于防御而非攻击。贝茨拟态指的是通过模仿危险生物来获得捕食者保护的动物，通常使用醒目的颜色。19世纪博物学家Henry Bates在注意到几种亚马逊蝴蝶物种看起来很像之后，首次提出了这种伪装技术。该技术后来以他的名字命名。在澳大利亚水域中，无毒的小丑蛇鳗有着与剧毒的黄唇海蛇相同的黑白条纹，确保没有捕食者会攻击它。然而，贝茨拟态的成功取决于模仿者与被模仿者的比例。澳大利亚博物馆的教育博物学家Martyn Robinson解释说，如果捕食者遇到太多可食用的模仿者，它就会认为带有这些标记的动物都不危险。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph F
passageNotes.text: 模仿更危险的生物不必完全精确，只需足以让潜在的捕食者犹豫即可。天蛾幼虫的腹部有类似蛇眼的斑纹。当受到威胁时，幼虫将头部缩回，“蛇眼”突然张开。究竟是潜在的捕食者认为自己看到了蛇，还是仅仅被吓了一跳，目前尚不清楚，但结果是幼虫活了下来，又看到了新的一天。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph G
passageNotes.text: 在昆士兰高原，变色守宫有另一种让捕食者犹豫的方式。它的身体是棕色的，但尾巴是黑白相间的条纹。Robinson解释说，如果受到攻击，变色守宫会断掉尾巴，尾巴会在地上扭动。许多蜥蜴都会这样做，但变色守宫的特殊之处在于，它的尾骨实际上会相互摩擦，因此会发出吱吱声。Robinson说：“捕食者当然会被地上这个黑白条纹的、扭动的、吱吱作响的东西完全吸引住，而守宫就可以悄悄溜走了。”这是一次性的把戏：重新长出的尾巴是棕色的，与守宫的身体颜色相同。这种精确的伪装和精心设计的诡计展示了大自然无限的可能性。但是，正如Robinson指出的，只有最成功的伪装大师才能在这里讲述这个故事。

items.text:
（1）题目 14：a species that indicates to its young to move to a place where they are less visible
题目翻译：一种会向幼崽发出信号、让它们移到不那么显眼位置的动物
答案：C
定位：正文 Section C
原文：When the chicks land, they are usually highly conspicuous, and their parents try to signal to them to move to a safe location.
译文：幼鸟落地时通常非常显眼，父母会设法向它们发出信号，让它们移到安全的位置。

解析：题干的 indicates to its young 对应 parents signal to them，less visible 对应从 highly conspicuous 的位置移到 safe location；这些信息集中在 C 段的茶色蛙口鸱幼鸟例子中。

（2）题目 15：an instance where sound is used to help an animal escape
题目翻译：一个利用声音帮助动物逃脱的例子
答案：G
定位：正文 Section G
原文：Many lizards do this, but in the case of the chameleon gecko the tail bones actually rub against one another, so it squeaks. ‘The predator is, of course, thoroughly absorbed by this black-and-white-striped, wriggling, squeaking thing on the ground, and the gecko can sneak away,’ Robinson says.
译文：许多蜥蜴都会断尾，但变色壁虎的尾骨会相互摩擦并发出吱吱声；捕食者被这条扭动、发声的尾巴完全吸引，壁虎便能悄悄逃走。

解析：G 段明确写尾巴会 squeak，声音连同扭动吸引捕食者，使壁虎能够 sneak away，完整对应“声音帮助动物逃脱”。

（3）题目 16：a creature that can use camouflage to match a range of different backgrounds
题目翻译：一种能用伪装适应多种不同背景的生物
答案：D
定位：正文 Section D
原文：The cuttlefish can almost instantly change its colour, pattern and texture to match its surroundings, using specialised cells and muscles.
译文：乌贼利用特殊细胞和肌肉，几乎能立刻改变颜色、图案和质地以匹配周围环境。

解析：D 段的乌贼能改变 colour、pattern 和 texture 来 match its surroundings，说明它能随不同环境调整伪装，而不是只适合一种固定背景。

（4）题目 17：a claim that the majority of animals disguise themselves in some way
题目翻译：一种关于大多数动物都会以某种方式伪装自己的说法
答案：A
定位：正文 Section A
原文：Most species use camouflage to some extent.
译文：大多数物种都会在某种程度上使用伪装。

解析：A 段首句直接给出概括性判断：Most species 对应 majority of animals，to some extent 对应 in some way。

（5）题目 18：examples of animals that use camouflage to look like plants
题目翻译：动物利用伪装使自己看起来像植物的例子
答案：B
定位：正文 Section B
原文：To that end, stick and leaf insects have evolved complex camouflage to hide themselves from predators. Many have the texture of sticks or dry leaves, while others imitate living foliage, even the veins in a leaf.
译文：竹节虫和叶虫进化出复杂伪装来躲避捕食者；许多具有树枝或枯叶的质感，另一些则模仿活叶，甚至连叶脉都仿得出来。

解析：B 段连续列举 stick and leaf insects，并说明它们模仿树枝、枯叶和活叶，正是动物伪装成植物的多个例子。

items.text:
（1）题目 19：one species has a camouflage tactic that is not present from birth.
题目翻译：某个物种的一种伪装策略并非出生时就具备。
答案：C
定位：正文 Section C
原文：Professor Gisela Kaplan of the University of New England in Australia says the frogmouth’s skill at camouflaging is learned behaviour. While adopting a pose may be a reflex of the bird, and can be observed in a hatchling’s first week, the ability to choose a backdrop which matches its colouration does not develop for 4–6 months.
译文：Gisela Kaplan 教授说，蛙口鸱的伪装技巧是习得行为；摆姿势可能是反射动作，但选择与自身颜色相配背景的能力要到四至六个月后才发展出来。

解析：not present from birth 对应 learned behaviour 和 does not develop for 4–6 months；提出这一观点的人是 Professor Gisela Kaplan，因此选 C。

（2）题目 20：species that live in an ancient environment have become very effective at camouflaging themselves.
题目翻译：生活在古老环境中的物种已经变得非常善于伪装。
答案：B
定位：正文 Section B
原文：‘It’s an incredibly old habitat, so the creatures have had a long time to adapt,’ Zborowski explains.
译文：Zborowski 解释说：“这是一个极其古老的生境，所以这些生物有很长时间来适应。”

解析：ancient environment 对应 incredibly old habitat，very effective at camouflaging 来自长期适应后的 convincingly disguised；说话者是 Paul Zborowski，因此选 B。

（3）题目 21：part of an animal is left behind to distract predators.
题目翻译：动物身体的一部分会被留下来转移捕食者的注意力。
答案：F
定位：正文 Section G
原文：Robinson explains that if attacked, the chameleon gecko will drop off its tail, which will wriggle around on the ground.
译文：Robinson 解释说，变色壁虎受到攻击时会断尾，尾巴会在地上继续扭动。

解析：drop off its tail 就是留下身体的一部分，随后捕食者被尾巴吸引；这一解释由 Martyn Robinson 提出，因此选 F。

（4）题目 22：if it takes too long to find one kind of prey, animals will look for an alternative source of food.
题目翻译：如果寻找一种猎物耗时太久，动物就会寻找另一种食物来源。
答案：A
定位：正文 Section A
原文：‘Camouflage increases the search time and, as a consequence, the predator will simply target another species, either because it doesn’t see the camouflaged individual or it just finds something more obvious to do.’
译文：伪装会增加搜索时间，因此捕食者会转而选择另一个物种：要么是没看见被伪装的个体，要么是发现了更容易下手的目标。

解析：takes too long 对应 increases the search time，alternative source of food 对应 target another species；提出这一原理的人是 Professor Mark Elgar，因此选 A。

（5）题目 23：camouflage can involve copying a threatening type of animal.
题目翻译：伪装可以包括模仿一种具有威胁性的动物。
答案：E
定位：正文 Section E
原文：Batesian mimicry refers to animals that gain protection from predators by imitating a dangerous organism, often using conspicuous colours. The nineteenth-century naturalist Henry Bates first suggested this camouflage technique after noticing that several Amazonian butterfly species looked the same.
译文：贝茨拟态指动物通过模仿危险生物来躲避捕食者，通常还会使用醒目的颜色；十九世纪博物学家 Henry Bates 首先提出了这种伪装方式。

解析：copying a threatening type of animal 对应 imitating a dangerous organism；原文随后说明该技巧由 Henry Bates 首先提出，因此选 E。

questionExplanations.text:
（1）题目 19：one species has a camouflage tactic that is not present from birth.
题目翻译：某个物种的一种伪装策略并非出生时就具备。
答案：C
定位：正文 Section C
原文：Professor Gisela Kaplan of the University of New England in Australia says the frogmouth’s skill at camouflaging is learned behaviour. While adopting a pose may be a reflex of the bird, and can be observed in a hatchling’s first week, the ability to choose a backdrop which matches its colouration does not develop for 4–6 months.
译文：Gisela Kaplan 教授说，蛙口鸱的伪装技巧是习得行为；摆姿势可能是反射动作，但选择与自身颜色相配背景的能力要到四至六个月后才发展出来。

解析：not present from birth 对应 learned behaviour 和 does not develop for 4–6 months；提出这一观点的人是 Professor Gisela Kaplan，因此选 C。

（2）题目 20：species that live in an ancient environment have become very effective at camouflaging themselves.
题目翻译：生活在古老环境中的物种已经变得非常善于伪装。
答案：B
定位：正文 Section B
原文：‘It’s an incredibly old habitat, so the creatures have had a long time to adapt,’ Zborowski explains.
译文：Zborowski 解释说：“这是一个极其古老的生境，所以这些生物有很长时间来适应。”

解析：ancient environment 对应 incredibly old habitat，very effective at camouflaging 来自长期适应后的 convincingly disguised；说话者是 Paul Zborowski，因此选 B。

（3）题目 21：part of an animal is left behind to distract predators.
题目翻译：动物身体的一部分会被留下来转移捕食者的注意力。
答案：F
定位：正文 Section G
原文：Robinson explains that if attacked, the chameleon gecko will drop off its tail, which will wriggle around on the ground.
译文：Robinson 解释说，变色壁虎受到攻击时会断尾，尾巴会在地上继续扭动。

解析：drop off its tail 就是留下身体的一部分，随后捕食者被尾巴吸引；这一解释由 Martyn Robinson 提出，因此选 F。

（4）题目 22：if it takes too long to find one kind of prey, animals will look for an alternative source of food.
题目翻译：如果寻找一种猎物耗时太久，动物就会寻找另一种食物来源。
答案：A
定位：正文 Section A
原文：‘Camouflage increases the search time and, as a consequence, the predator will simply target another species, either because it doesn’t see the camouflaged individual or it just finds something more obvious to do.’
译文：伪装会增加搜索时间，因此捕食者会转而选择另一个物种：要么是没看见被伪装的个体，要么是发现了更容易下手的目标。

解析：takes too long 对应 increases the search time，alternative source of food 对应 target another species；提出这一原理的人是 Professor Mark Elgar，因此选 A。

（5）题目 23：camouflage can involve copying a threatening type of animal.
题目翻译：伪装可以包括模仿一种具有威胁性的动物。
答案：E
定位：正文 Section E
原文：Batesian mimicry refers to animals that gain protection from predators by imitating a dangerous organism, often using conspicuous colours. The nineteenth-century naturalist Henry Bates first suggested this camouflage technique after noticing that several Amazonian butterfly species looked the same.
译文：贝茨拟态指动物通过模仿危险生物来躲避捕食者，通常还会使用醒目的颜色；十九世纪博物学家 Henry Bates 首先提出了这种伪装方式。

解析：copying a threatening type of animal 对应 imitating a dangerous organism；原文随后说明该技巧由 Henry Bates 首先提出，因此选 E。

items.text:
（1）题目 24：Dr Karen Cheney studies the bluestriped fangblenny on ________ off Queensland’s coast. She found that the fangblenny was able to make itself resemble other fish by adjusting its colouration. The fangblenny impersonates the striped cleaner wrasse, a fish that is welcomed by other species as it gets rid of their ________. The fangblenny can approach its ________ without drawing the attention of predators or disturbing the work of the striped cleaner wrasse.
题目翻译：Karen Cheney 博士在昆士兰海岸外的 ______ 上研究蓝纹鳚。
答案：reefs
定位：正文 Section D
原文：On Queensland’s reefs, scientists have been studying another ocean dweller that uses colour change, although not to blend into the surroundings.
译文：在昆士兰的珊瑚礁上，科学家一直在研究另一种会变色的海洋生物，不过它变色并不是为了融入周围环境。

解析：题干把 On Queensland’s reefs 改写为 on ___ off Queensland’s coast，地点名词保持为复数 reefs，填入后语法和地点关系都完整。

（2）题目 25：Dr Karen Cheney studies the bluestriped fangblenny on ________ off Queensland’s coast. She found that the fangblenny was able to make itself resemble other fish by adjusting its colouration. The fangblenny impersonates the striped cleaner wrasse, a fish that is welcomed by other species as it gets rid of their ________. The fangblenny can approach its ________ without drawing the attention of predators or disturbing the work of the striped cleaner wrasse.
题目翻译：清洁隆头鱼受到其他物种欢迎，因为它会清除它们身上的 ______。
答案：parasites
定位：正文 Section D
原文：Its most impressive impersonation is of the black-with-neon-blue-striped cleaner wrasse, which eats the parasites on larger fish.
译文：它模仿得最像的是带黑色与荧光蓝条纹的清洁隆头鱼，这种鱼会吃掉大型鱼身上的寄生虫。

解析：题干的 gets rid of 对应原文 eats，their 指 larger fish；被清除的是 parasites，因此空格填原文复数名词。

（3）题目 26：Dr Karen Cheney studies the bluestriped fangblenny on ________ off Queensland’s coast. She found that the fangblenny was able to make itself resemble other fish by adjusting its colouration. The fangblenny impersonates the striped cleaner wrasse, a fish that is welcomed by other species as it gets rid of their ________. The fangblenny can approach its ________ without drawing the attention of predators or disturbing the work of the striped cleaner wrasse.
题目翻译：蓝纹鳚能够在不引起捕食者注意、也不干扰清洁隆头鱼工作的情况下接近它的 ______。
答案：prey
定位：正文 Section D
原文：Not only does the fangblenny benefit from the reduced predation that comes with the wrasse’s beneficial relationships with other fish, but the disguise also lets it get closer to prey.
译文：蓝纹鳚不仅因清洁隆头鱼与其他鱼类的互利关系而减少被捕食的风险，这种伪装还让它更接近猎物。

解析：原文说伪装既减少 predators 带来的威胁，也让蓝纹鳚更接近 prey；题干询问它能够接近的对象，因此填 prey。
